answer: Agents admit a new identity only after it posts a slashable bond and earns a reputation through escrowed trades. Existing agents randomly challenge claims; a failed or colluding identity loses its bond, while honest partners gain payment and credibility. Sybil influence therefore requires capital for every fake account and risks repeated forfeiture, so creating hundreds of identities becomes expensive. An inlet may attract newcomers, but no haven protects them from audits recorded in the shared atlas.
